jobs.title: National Director, Credit Structuring ( Real Estate Finance)
jobs.description:
The Real Estate Financing team operates within BMO’s Canadian Commercial Banking division and supports privately held companies engaged in real estate construction and development. The team is accountable for driving revenue growth, managing and monitoring loan portfolios, meeting credit requirements, and supporting cross‑selling across our broader business. We assess financing opportunities ranging from $10,000,000 to over $1,000,000,000.

Analyzes credit information to support lending decisions and processes for new and existing Commercial banking loans and credit solutions in an assigned portfolio of clients. Makes credit decisions and recommendations in compliance with bank policies and procedures while maintaining an exceptional client service environment.

Leverages advanced deal structuring expertise to negotiate loan terms and conditions and structure loans balancing client requirements with the bank’s risk appetite and policies.
In alignment with credit qualifications, signs off on new, renewal and extension loans.
Conducts comprehensive portfolio monitoring and performance analysis including covenant compliance and client industry trends to identify risks and opportunities.
Leads the development and implementation of advanced capital allocation strategies, that leverage market insights and portfolio analysis and optimize investment returns.
Oversees financial and risk analysis to make informed credit-granting decisions and assessments of portfolio health
Handles escalated client concerns and service requests, ensuring expectations are consistently met or exceeded.
Builds and maintains a portfolio of strong relationships that ensures a superior client experience and drives financial performance.
Leads complex proposal development and delivers presentations to acquire clients or win business.
Advises on strategic business priorities, resource allocation, and change initiatives to ensure successful execution of key strategies across commercial banking functions.
Engages with industry peers and networks to gather competitive insights and best practices, applying this knowledge to maintain a competitive edge.
Builds and maintains client relationships to ensure long-term financial performance in collaboration with Relationship Manager and business partners.
Structures and supports new, renewal and extension loans aligned with client needs and bank & risk policies
Conducts financial analysis and risk assessments of clients’ credit information, for an assigned portfolio, to provide insights and make informed decisions
Monitors the portfolio performance for assigned portfolio of Commercial Banking clients on an ongoing basis, taking corrective action when required.
Minimizes BMO’s risk exposure by adhering to credit policies, regulatory standards, and operational guidelines.
Serves as a point of contact for service requests, ensuring expectations are consistently met or exceeded. Escalates issues when needed.
Supports and implements initiatives to enhance service quality, acquire new business and expand client relationships.
Identifies revenue and cross-selling opportunities to enhance portfolio growth.
Identifies share of wallet opportunities.
Leverages analysis tools to nurture and grow a portfolio that exceeds ROE thresholds and evaluates client returns on a proactive basis.
Manages timely and accurate data entry into BMO's systems and leverages the data to support decision-making.
Fosters a culture aligned to BMO purpose, values and strategy and role models BMO values and behaviours in all that they do.
Ensures alignment between values and behaviour that fosters diversity and inclusion.
Regularly connects work to BMO’s purpose, sets inspirational goals, defines clear expected outcomes, and ensures clear accountability for follow through.
Builds interdependent teams that collaborate across functional and operating groups to create the highest value for all stakeholders.
Attracts, retains, and enables the career development of top talent.
Improves team performance, recognizes and rewards performance, coaches employees, supports their development, and manages poor performance.
Advises clients and prospects on sophisticated financial solutions and tailored strategic recommendations.
Operates at a group/enterprise-wide level and serves as a senior specialist resource across BMO.
Influences how teams/groups work together.
Applies expertise and thinks creatively to address unique or ambiguous situations and to find solutions to multiple, interdependent, complex problems.
Communicates abstract concepts in simple terms.
Fosters strong internal and external networks and works with and across multiple teams to achieve business objectives.
Anticipates trends and responds by implementing appropriate changes.
Broader work or accountabilities may be assigned as needed.
Take measured risks while protecting the bank by applying our Risk Management Framework in the execution of your role, in line with our Risk Culture and within our approved Risk Appetite, making sound and risk informed decisions that align to business strategy, protect assets, and adhere to applicable policy documents (Frameworks, Policies, Standards, Procedures and Supporting documents), laws and regulations.

Qualifications:

Preferred 9+ years of relevant experience in credit or lending instruments or financial operations in a corporate or banking environment.
Bachelor’s degree required, Master’s degree preferred; Business Administration, Finance and Accounting preferred. Any other related discipline or commensurate work experience considered.
If a Credit Qualifiable job, Credit Qualifications and associated credit knowledge and skills according to the credit portfolio requirements and qualification standards.
Seasoned expert with extensive industry knowledge.
Technical leader viewed as a thought leader for innovation.

Advanced level of proficiency:

Structuring Deals
Change Management
Problem Solving
People Management
Detail-Oriented
Leadership
Loan Structuring
Regulatory Compliance
Portfolio Management
Credit Risk Assessment
Banking Operations

Expert level of proficiency:

Customer Service
Financial analysis
Microsoft Office

Salary:

$120,000.00 - $215,000.00

Pay Type:

Salaried

The above represents BMO Financial Group’s pay range and type.

Salaries will vary based on factors such as location, skills, experience, education, and qualifications for the role, and may include a commission structure. Salaries for part-time roles will be pro-rated based on number of hours regularly worked. For commission roles, the salary listed above represents BMO Financial Group’s expected target for the first year in this position.

BMO Financial Group’s total compensation package will vary based on the pay type of the position and may include performance-based incentives, discretionary bonuses, as well as other perks and rewards. BMO also offers health insurance, tuition reimbursement, accident and life insurance, and retirement savings plans. To view more details of our benefits, please visit: https://jobs.bmo.com/global/en/Total-Rewards

At BMO we are driven by a shared Purpose: Boldly Grow the Good in business and life. It calls on us to create lasting, positive change for our customers, our communities and our people. By working together, innovating and pushing boundaries, we transform lives and businesses, and power economic growth around the world.

As a member of the BMO team you are valued, respected and heard, and you have more ways to grow and make an impact. We strive to help you make an impact from day one – for yourself and our customers. jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer (CFO) Strategic Business Executive
jobs.description:
Come... Enjoy... Work
in a fast paced, dynamic environment. Located on the Tsuut’ina First Nation, Grey Eagle Resort & Casino is Calgary’s number one entertainment facility. We are looking for talented, energetic and motivated individuals to join our diverse workforce! We offer competitive salaries, benefits and opportunities to grow your career.

Position Overview

The Chief Financial Officer (CFO) is a key executive leader responsible for the financial stewardship, strategic planning, governance support, and long-term sustainability of Grey Eagle Resort & Casino (GERC).

Reporting directly to the Board of Directors, the CFO serves as the principal financial advisor to the Board and Executive Leadership Team, providing leadership across financial operations, capital investment planning, enterprise risk management, business growth initiatives, and stakeholder relations.

The CFO plays a critical role in supporting the Board's vision for sustainable economic growth while protecting and enhancing the assets of Grey Eagle Resort & Casino for future generations of the Tsuut'ina Nation.

The role oversees all financial functions and provides executive leadership for major capital projects, resort renovations, business development initiatives, financing strategies, and governance matters affecting the organization.

As one of the most senior leaders within GERC, the CFO must balance strategic thinking, operational understanding, financial discipline, and relationship-building with a diverse group of stakeholders including the Board of Directors, Tsuut'ina Nation leadership, regulators, financial institutions, development partners, and operational leaders.

Education And Experience

CPA designation.
Bachelor's Degree in Accounting, Finance, Commerce, or related discipline.
Minimum 10 years progressive financial leadership experience.
Minimum 5 years in a senior executive role.
Experience in hospitality, gaming, resort, entertainment, tourism, real estate development, or similarly complex operations.
Experience reporting directly to a Board of Directors.
Experience leading major capital projects exceeding $10M.
Demonstrated success managing banking and financing relationships.

Preferred

MBA or Master's Degree.
Experience working with Indigenous-owned organizations, governments, or economic development entities.
Experience in a regulated gaming environment.
Experience supporting Board committees and governance functions.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Strategic Leadership & Board Support

Serve as the primary financial advisor to the Board of Directors.
Provide recommendations on strategic initiatives, capital investments, financing structures, business growth opportunities, and organizational performance.
Prepare and present comprehensive financial and operational reports to the Board.
Support the Board in strategic planning and long-term sustainability initiatives.
Participate in governance discussions and provide financial guidance regarding organizational priorities.
Assist the Board in evaluating significant business opportunities, acquisitions, partnerships, and development projects.

________________________________________

Financial Leadership & Stewardship

Lead all aspects of financial management and reporting.
Develop and execute financial strategies aligned with organizational goals.
Oversee:
Budgeting, Forecasting, Financial Reporting
Treasury Management, Cash Flow Management
Internal Controls
Tax Compliance
Audit Functions
Capital Planning
Ensure financial integrity and accountability throughout the organization.
Establish and monitor key performance indicators and financial metrics.

________________________________________

Capital Projects, Renovation & Development Oversight

The CFO will provide executive leadership for capital investment planning and project governance across the resort.

Responsibilities Include

Develop long-term capital investment strategies.
Oversee financial planning and governance for renovation and expansion projects.
Lead financial evaluation and business case development for all major capital expenditures.
Monitor project budgets, timelines, risks, and return on investment.
Ensure appropriate project controls and reporting mechanisms are in place.

________________________________________

Master Site Development Planning

Participate in long-term master planning for Grey Eagle Resort & Casino lands and facilities.
Evaluate future development opportunities through financial modeling and strategic analysis.
Support land use planning, phased development initiatives, and infrastructure investment decisions.
Provide financial leadership related to future resort expansion opportunities.
Collaborate with Nation leadership, developers, consultants, and external advisors regarding future growth initiatives.

________________________________________

Banking, Financing & Capital Structure Management

Lead relationships with financial institutions and lending partners.
Develop financing strategies to support operational and capital requirements.
Negotiate banking agreements, credit facilities, and financing arrangements.
Manage cash reserves and liquidity planning.
Advise the Board regarding capital structure optimization and debt management strategies.

________________________________________

Hotel Asset Management & Resort Performance

Provide strategic oversight regarding the financial performance of hotel and resort assets.
Evaluate asset performance and investment priorities.
Support lifecycle planning for hotel, gaming, entertainment, and food & beverage facilities.
Monitor asset utilization and return on investment.
Develop recommendations regarding reinvestment and asset enhancement opportunities.

________________________________________

Casino Reinvestment Strategy

Develop and maintain a long-term casino reinvestment strategy.
Assess gaming floor performance and capital replacement needs.
Support strategic decisions regarding gaming technology and facility improvements.
Ensure reinvestment planning aligns with market conditions and guest expectations.
Evaluate opportunities to enhance competitiveness and profitability.

________________________________________

iGaming Strategy, Financial Oversight & Business Development

Provide executive financial leadership for the establishment, launch, growth, and ongoing financial performance of GERC's iGaming business unit.
Lead financial modelling, budgeting, forecasting, capital planning, and business-case evaluation related to iGaming operations and strategic initiatives.
Establish and oversee appropriate financial reporting, revenue assurance, reconciliation, treasury, payment processing, settlement, and internal control frameworks for iGaming activities.
Develop and monitor key iGaming performance indicators, including Gross Gaming Revenue (GGR), Net Gaming Revenue (NGR), gaming margins, customer acquisition costs, promotional and bonus costs, player value, deposits and withdrawals, chargebacks, operating costs, and profitability.
Work collaboratively with iGaming leadership, Compliance, Legal, Information Technology, Cybersecurity, Marketing, and Operations to ensure appropriate financial governance and risk management.
Ensure financial processes, controls, reporting, and recordkeeping support applicable regulatory requirements and GERC's obligations to Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis (AGLC) and the Alberta iGaming Corporation (AiGC).
Provide financial oversight of banking arrangements, payment service providers, gaming technology providers, platform vendors, and other significant iGaming commercial relationships.
Evaluate future iGaming products, partnerships, technology investments, and business expansion opportunities from a financial and strategic perspective.

________________________________________

Procurement Governance

Establish financial oversight and governance for procurement activities.
Ensure transparency, accountability, and value-for-money principles.
Develop policies and controls supporting major purchasing initiatives.
Participate in evaluation and approval processes for significant contracts and vendor relationships.
Ensure procurement activities align with Board-approved financial policies.

________________________________________

Indigenous Relations & Partnership Development

Build and maintain respectful relationships with Tsuut'ina Nation leadership and stakeholders.
Support initiatives that align with the Nation's economic development goals.
Identify opportunities for strategic partnerships that advance organizational objectives.
Participate in partnership discussions with Indigenous and non-Indigenous organizations.
Ensure financial strategies reflect the values and long-term interests of ownership.

Team Members

Consultants and Contractors

Ensure effective internal controls and compliance programs.
Support Board governance and Finance & Audit Committee activities.
Oversee annual external audits.
Ensure compliance with all applicable laws, regulations, and accounting standards.
Develop financial risk mitigation strategies.

Presenting financial results and forecasts.

Reporting on compliance and internal controls.
Supporting governance best practices.

jobs.title: Head, Managing Director -Wealth Planning, Private Wealth Canada
jobs.description:
Leads and manages the provision of specialized and advanced wealth planning, guidance and counsel to BMO’s Personal Wealth Distribution businesses (Private Wealth Canada). Leverages extensive experience in leading planning professionals and utilizes deep technical planning expertise to motivate and challenge a team of advanced planning professionals with expertise in tax, estate and trust, business advisory & succession planning and philanthropy. Provides advanced planning services to HNW and UHNW clients and supports all frontline professionals who are delivering planning within Personal Wealth ensuring they have access to ongoing resources, tools and systems to assist in complex planning issues. Develops a strategy to ensure BMO has leading and competitive capabilities in specialized planning to meet the complex and comprehensive needs of HNW and UHNW clients. Leads a centre of expertise, building and executing BMO’s strategy to be a thought leader internally and externally around wealth planning across North America. Develops and leads the distribution and sales support strategy to ensure specialized planning knowledge is leveraged by the other professionals within the function and frontline professionals. Develops and drives the strategic plan for the delivery of best in class specialized wealth planning services and sets the groundwork to ensure the needs of HNW and UHNW clients are optimally met by partnering with lead relationship managers in WM and other LoBs, and where appropriate other external professionals and Centres of Influence. Collaborate across BMO to identify cross LOB business opportunities leveraging specialized planning team.

Become the growth engine of Private Wealth Canada by identifying significant wealth management opportunities such as investment, insurance, trust, lending and other revenue sources through holistic sophisticated wealth planning delivery engagements.
Provides overall leadership and strategic direction to the Specialized Wealth Planning Team by setting context and direction, defining accountabilities, tasks and assignments and establishing boundaries for decision-making and approvals.
Coaches, motivates, develops and evaluates performance of specialized planning leaders and provides guidance and mentoring to those direct reports in the resolution of complex issues
Establishes and maintains a sales management process to ensure opportunities for portfolio growth and profile enhancement are maximized including: maximizing the expertise of internal partners; establishing and strengthening relationships with other sales forces; recognizing referral opportunities to BMO Financial Group partners
Partners with key groups such as NA Commercial Banking to identify cross business referral opportunities through leveraging specialized resources. Partners with colleagues in the U.S. , if required, to ensure cross border planning expertise is being leveraged to meet clients’ North American planning needs.
Ensures consistent communication of strategy and messaging between Enterprise Wealth Planning and the LOBs
Hold employees accountable to their business/sales plans; conducts thorough performance assessments; coaches and provides candid feedback; ensures alignment of rewards to objectives, alignment with team and to BMO Financial Group values
Instills collaborative approach to ensure team members partner with colleagues in Enterprise Wealth Planning and across BMO Financial Group in providing financial solutions to clients
Partners with Wealth Planning Leaders and Market Leaders to recruit, develop and promote a high performing planning team in order to provide the leadership and bench strength necessary over the long-term to meet Wealth Managements strategic business and growth objectives
Partners with market leadership to ensure each market has access to the specific specialized planning support required
Develops talent strategy and ongoing pipeline for specialized planning professionals for Personal Wealth
Leads the development and guides the implementation of the strategy to provide advanced and specialized planning advice and services within Wealth Management
Partners with the Wealth Management leadership to develop the engagement and delivery model of overall planning support for high value clients
Assesses and approves external experts qualified to provide advisors with tax and estate planning services
Provides front line sales force with accurate and detailed subject matter expertise in all areas of wealth management
Serves as in-house expert in providing financial planning support on technical issues in the areas of investment planning, education planning, retirement planning and transition planning, with general knowledge of estate planning, personal taxation and insurance.
Promotes the services of the HNW Consulting & Financial Planning strategy of technical experts across Personal Wealth
Ensures team is knowledgeable on wealth products and services (including advice content, process and tools) and have a general understanding of the products and services across BMO Financial Group and its partners
Provides SME and thought leadership regarding selection/development of tools and technology platforms to be utilized by wealth planning professionals
Contributes to the building of the Enterprise Centre of Expertise for Wealth Planning (processes, workflow, delivery strategy), specifically in terms of the HNW and UHNW client segments for BMO Personal Wealth
Establishes baselines and KPIs for measuring planning performance such as client penetration metrics, number of plans completed, client satisfaction surveys, retention statistics, plan quality metrics, etc.
Provides insight and share expertise with team members for advanced financial planning concepts, such as, succession planning and philanthropy and other complex wealth services offerings.
Provides oversight and handles all escalations from team on complex deals, provide insight and direction to team members, experts and IAs on best course of action
Partners with all Wealth Management discipline heads and other partners across BMO Financial Group to provide a broad-based solutions approach for specific client situations.
Partners with distribution leadership to develop local strategies to increase adoption of wealth planning and increase number households with financial plans
Develops internal and external networks and referrals sources to ensure the ongoing growth of the Wealth Management business to achieve identified targets
Demonstrates a consultative and collaborative selling approach in customer conversations, acting as a member of a client team, to facilitate the desired Wealth Management client experience and to achieve business goals
Provides proactive, integrated, and customized advice and creates and implements wealth planning strategies to help clients achieve their financial and personal goals
Protects BMO Financial Group’s assets by adhering to all banking, investment and lending regulations (as appropriate), Policies and Procedures, legal and ethical requirements, process requirements, BMO Financial Group guidelines and established risk guidelines
Build the framework for an effective quality review process of plans delivered.
Adhere to and maintain professional designations as per Regulatory bodies
Within the mandate of this role, promotes and supports the Bank’s risk culture including ensuring employees understand their accountabilities for risk-taking activities, promoting an environment of open communication and effective challenge, and establishing the “tone from the top” through leading by example.
Takes measured risks while protecting the bank by applying our Risk Management Framework in the execution of their role, in line with our Risk Culture and within our approved Risk Appetite, making sound and risk informed decisions that align to business strategy, protect assets, and adhere to applicable policy documents (Frameworks, Policies, Standards, Procedures and Supporting documents), laws and regulations.
Role models driving simplicity and productivity enhancements for optimization across groups, driving continuous improvement on key measures.
Activates our winning culture, aligned with Purpose. Ignites engagement by aligning our culture to our strategy and fueling exceptional execution.
Fosters an inclusive environment for all employees by eliminating barriers to inclusion.
Develops leaders, plans for succession, and fosters a high-performance culture.
Drives top talent acquisition and retention, developing organizational capabilities to drive competitive advantage.
Leads and mentors a team with diverse risk and business experience, skills, and orientation.
Leads, promotes, and reinforces the Bank’s Ambition; personally, role models One Bank leadership; drives sustainable improvements in customer loyalty and business growth; adheres and supports enterprise customer experience and brand standards.

Qualifications:

Post-secondary education, preferably with business orientation; MBA an asset
10+ years of experience providing financial planning services or advice as a senior financial planner
Strong business acumen with the ability to connect planning activity to client acquisition, client retention, revenue growth, share of wallet and ROE.
Strategic, enterprise-minded leader who can set direction, simplify complexity and translate strategy into clear execution.
Change leadership capability, including the ability to drive adoption, shift behaviours, challenge legacy practices and sustain momentum across a national business.
Canadian Securities Course or higher securities industry designation
CA/CPA, CGA/CMA, LLB/LL.L/LL.M or other professional wealth designations an asset
CLU, R.F.P., CSWP, TED, FCSI, FMA, CIM designations
CFP Designation required and/or Personal Financial Planner designation (ICB)
Experience managing a team of advanced planning professionals
Knowledge of financial planning principles and standards
Specific knowledge of Taxation, Estates, Trust and Insurance
Possess broad and diverse knowledge of the investment business and the Bank’s overall products, services, systems and distribution channels
Financial services sales experience
Exceptional relationship management, sales and service orientation
Strong Interpersonal skills and managerial leadership skills
Exceptional oral and written communication skills
Ability to clearly communicate complex planning advice issues in a comprehensive and practical manner
Influencing skills (uses direct and indirect strategies to persuade and provide advice)
Ability to think strategically, creatively and resolve complex and ambiguous problems
Exceptional networking, presentation, facilitation, and relationship building skills
Surrounding knowledge of areas with in Taxation, Estates Trust - deem specific examples

jobs.title: Managing Director, Corporate Finance Group
jobs.description:
Facilitates growth for the Bank through business development and management of key client relationships. Maintains an outstanding and continuous record of significant revenue generation from sales and syndications.

Acts as an escalation point for complex client issues, using strategic problem-solving to resolve conflicts and maintaining strong client relationships.
Leads the structuring of high-value, complex deals, and credit approvals, ensuring alignment with client needs.
Oversees credit approvals and drives pricing coordination, acting as the primary client advocate to ensure alignment with client needs and bank objectives.
Drives negotiations for high-value, complex transactions and credit approvals, ensuring deals are structured to meet client needs.
Manages high-value client portfolios, driving cross-selling, retention, and profitability.
Implements cross-selling initiatives, driving client engagement and successfully transitioning opportunities into revenue-generating sales.
Leads market coverage strategies to expand portfolios, identify opportunities, and align with business goals.
Represents bank at industry forums and conferences, leveraging insights on trends, competition, and emerging products to drive strategic decision-making.
Engages with senior leadership and cross-functional teams to align strategies, address client needs, and drive holistic business solutions.
Delivers reports to the bank’s leadership on team performance, client satisfaction, market trends, and key strategic initiatives, delivering insights that inform corporate strategy.
Drives strategic advisory on loan products, options, rates, terms, and collateral requirements, ensuring tailored solutions that align with client needs and business objectives.
Builds and maintains strong long-term relationships with the bank’s high-value and strategic clients, providing strategic advice on financial solutions and ensuring exceptional service and partnership.
Structures deals, secures credit approvals, negotiates high-value transactions, and identifies opportunities for cross-selling.
Analyzes market trends, client industry developments, and competitive positioning to inform client solution strategies and optimize client satisfaction.
Works closely with internal teams and stakeholders to define products, solutions and strategies that best fit clients’ needs.
Identifies share of wallet opportunities.
Leverages analysis tools to nurture and grow a portfolio that exceeds ROE thresholds and evaluates client returns on a proactive basis.
Ensures adherence to regulatory requirements, internal controls, and compliance policies in all aspects of relationship management, mitigating risk and maintaining service standards.
Fosters a culture aligned to BMO purpose, values and strategy and role models BMO values and behaviours in all that they do.
Ensures alignment between values and behaviour that fosters diversity and inclusion.
Regularly connects work to BMO’s purpose, sets inspirational goals, defines clear expected outcomes, and ensures clear accountability for follow through.
Builds interdependent teams that collaborate across functional and operating groups to create the highest value for all stakeholders.
Attracts, retains, and enables the career development of top talent.
Improves team performance, recognizes and rewards performance, coaches employees, supports their development, and manages poor performance.
Operates at a group/enterprise-wide level and serves as a specialist resource to senior leaders and stakeholders.
Applies expertise and thinks creatively to address unique or ambiguous situations and to find solutions to problems that can be complex and non-routine.
Implements changes in response to shifting trends.
Broader work or accountabilities may be assigned as needed.
Take measured risks while protecting the bank by applying our Risk Management Framework in the execution of your role, in line with our Risk Culture and within our approved Risk Appetite, making sound and risk informed decisions that align to business strategy, protect assets, and adhere to applicable policy documents (Frameworks, Policies, Standards, Procedures and Supporting documents), laws and regulations.

Qualifications:

10+ years of relevant experience in Relationship Management, Account Management or Portfolio Management in a corporate or similar segmented banking environment with sales metrics is preferred.
Bachelor’s degree required; Business Administration, Finance and Accounting preferred. Any other related discipline or commensurate work experience considered.
If a Credit Qualifiable role, Credit Qualifications and associated credit knowledge and skills according to the credit portfolio requirements and qualification standards.
Seasoned professional with a combination of education, experience and industry knowledge.

Advanced level of proficiency:

Project Management
Change Management
People Management

Expert level of proficiency:

Product Knowledge
Regulatory Compliance
Structuring Deals
Portfolio Management
Credit Risk Assessment
Customer Service
Stakeholder Management
Negotiation
Customer Relationship Building

new_jobs.title: AI & Data Utilities Leader
new_jobs.description:
We Are:

Accenture Data & AI — the people who love using data to tell a story. We're the world's largest team of data scientists and experts in machine learning and AI. A great day for us means solving big problems using the latest tech, serious brain power, and deep knowledge of just about every industry. We believe a mix of data, analytics, automation, and responsible AI can do almost anything — spark digital reinvention, widen the range of what humans can do, and breathe life into smart products and services.

In the Public Sector, we partner with government agencies, crown corporations, and public institutions to drive meaningful, citizen-centred transformation. We bring the full depth of Accenture's AI and data capabilities to solve complex challenges that matter at a societal scale.

You Are: A thought leader and practitioner at the intersection of AI strategy and data delivery — As a senior leader in the Data & AI practice, you will coach and mentor up-and-coming leaders, guide diverse multi-disciplinary teams, and help clients embed AI and data capabilities as a lasting part of their organisational culture — with a strong focus on responsible AI, data governance, and public trust.

Role Summary

As a Senior Leader
in Accenture’s Data &AI
practice, you will lead the strategy, design, and scaled delivery of AI & Data solutions for Utilities
industry and clients
. You will build reusable data/AI capabilities—covering ingestion, orchestration, governance, data products, analytics enablement, and model/AI lifecycle—so clients can accelerate time-to-value while meeting enterprise-grade requirements for security, privacy, quality, and responsible AI. The Utilities industry is at the center of the largest infrastructure transformation in a generation—the collision of decarbonization, unprecedented load growth from electrification and data centers, grid resilience against extreme weather events, affordability and regulatory pressure, and the shift to distributed, digitized, AI-enabled operations. You will own the Data & AI agenda for our Utilities portfolio across Canada, personally leading the most consequential CxO relationships, and set the pace for how the portfolio grows, delivers and shows up in the market.

Key Responsibilities

Set direction for AI & Data Utilities: Own the target-state vision, architecture, and roadmap for data/AI utilities across complex enterprise landscapes (multiple systems, domains, and stakeholders).

Lead large-scale client engagements: Drive end-to-end delivery leadership across strategy, design, build, and transition-to-run, ensuring outcomes and adoption.

Operationalize reusable accelerators: Establish standards and scalable patterns (reference architectures, reusable pipelines, governance workflows, data product frameworks, and MLOps/LLMOps practices).

Governance & responsible AI leadership: Ensure data governance, lineage, quality, access controls, privacy/security-by-design, and responsible AI practices are embedded into utility capabilities.

Client & executive stakeholder management: Lead executive communications, manage relationships with CIO/CTO/CDAO/Operations leadership, and align delivery to business outcomes and enterprise priorities.

People leadership & talent development: Lead and mentor multi-disciplinary teams (architecture, engineering, data operations, analytics/AI, delivery), ensuring strong delivery rigor and continuous improvement.

Commercial ownership and growth support: Contribute to proposal development, shape solution approaches, estimate effort, and support expansion within industry/enterprise accounts.

Delivery governance: Ensure quality, risk management, and delivery health across workstreams; manage dependencies, budgets (where applicable), and escalations.

Shape the Utilities Data & AI agenda: own the industry point of view and go-to-market, including energy-transition advisory, rate case and regulatory environment, OT/IT convergence, grid-modernization and DERMS-enabling data platforms, wildfire and resilience analytics, customer-experience transformation and AI-enabled workforce and field operations. Represent Accenture externally with clients, alliance partners, regulators and industry bodies.

Bachelor's or master's degree in computer science, business administration, commerce, or engineering

12+ years of relevant experience in enterprise data platforms and/or AI/ML engineering, including architecture and operationalization.

Proven track record of building and growing an industry portfolio – origination, sales and expansion – with personally attributable multi-$MM record in annual originated sales and ownership of multi-$MM in managed revenue at portfolio scale, sustained across multiple years and through all least one full economic or industry cycle.

Recognized trusted advisor to C-suite and Board-level executives at large enterprise Utility industry clients, with the credibility and presence to lead the most challenging conversations on strategy, investment, and transformation outcomes in a rapidly changing Utilities landscape.

Demonstrated experience leading large, multi-year transformation programs with measurable outcomes (platform adoption, performance improvement, reduced time-to-insight, improved operational efficiency, etc.).

Strong background in enterprise data architecture and delivery for utility-style platforms (integration, orchestration, data products, governance, and data operations).

Proven leadership in MLOps/LLMOps and lifecycle management (deployment, monitoring, evaluation, governance, and continual improvement).

Deep understanding of data governance (quality, lineage, catalog, access controls) and responsible AI (risk controls, evaluation, auditability, transparency principles).

Strong experience in stakeholder and executive management and ability to translate technical strategy into business value.

Track record of building, leading & developing high-performance teams at scale and influencing without authority across client organizations and internal leadership.

Recognized eminence and thought leadership in Data & AI for Utilities – evidenced by such recurring keynote or mainstage presence at flagship industry forums (e.g. DistribuTECH, CERAWeek, Enlit, WEF Energy), published points of view carried by tier-one industry or business media in the last 24 months, and standing relationships with the leading Utilities in Canada as well as AI/Data analysts (Gartner, Forrester, Wood Mackenzie, S&P Global).

Skills & Experience (Preferred)

Familiarity with industrial/enterprise contexts aligned to I&E (manufacturing, industrial operations, industrial IoT/data, maintenance & reliability analytics, supply chain/asset performance).

Direct senior-client experience across at least two of: North American Utilities & Power companies, European integrated utilities and network operators, and Asia-Pacific power, water or renewables majors.

Experience with cloud-based data and AI platforms (e.g., Azure/AWS/GCP), data engineering frameworks, CI/CD, observability, and automation practices.

Experience delivering batch + streaming data solutions and integrating enterprise systems (ETL/ELT, APIs, event streaming, integration frameworks).

Hands-on or strong working knowledge of data/AI tooling for orchestration, feature/data management, and governance workflows.

Travel / Working Conditions (Typical)

May require travel depending on client needs (industry/enterprise engagements).

Combination of client collaboration and remote delivery.

new_jobs.description:
Accelerate your success at Colliers.

Why Colliers?

As one of Canada’s leading commercial real estate services firms, we are driven by our mission to accelerate success for our people, clients, and communities.

A career at Colliers gives you the opportunity to make an impact, advance your career, and collaborate with top-tier talent. Don’t just take our word for it – we’ve been recognized as a top employer on a number of prestigious lists, including Best Workplaces in Canada, Best Workplaces with Most Trusted Executive Teams, among others.

Toronto, ON, Hybrid

About The Role

As Director, Data Engineering within our Global Technology & Data Team, you'll play a pivotal role in shaping and executing Colliers' enterprise data engineering strategy across a complex multi-cloud environment. Partnering closely with data leadership, enterprise architecture, and technology stakeholders, you will lead the design, delivery, and operation of scalable data platforms and services that enable business transformation, advanced analytics, artificial intelligence, and data-driven decision making across North America and globally.

This is an opportunity to leverage your expertise to help drive Colliers' next-generation data ecosystem, modernize our enterprise data platforms, and position the organization for continued innovation and growth.

Lead enterprise data engineering strategy: Direct and scale a high-performing team of managers and data engineers, fostering a culture of innovation, collaboration, continuous improvement, and technical excellence.
Drive modern data platform delivery: Oversee the design, development, and implementation of enterprise-scale data platforms, including microservices architectures, data mesh and data fabric capabilities, AI/ML pipelines, Agentic AI and GenAI workflows, document extraction services, and business intelligence solutions.
Champion technology roadmap and innovation: Partner with Enterprise Architecture, product leaders, vendors, and technology stakeholders to define and execute the long-term data engineering roadmap, ensuring alignment with regional and global business objectives.
Establish operational excellence and DataOps practices: Define and enforce standards for DataOps, SDLC, CI/CD, data governance, security, documentation, code quality, and AI-enabled delivery methodologies to ensure scalable and reliable platform operations.
Ensure platform reliability and service excellence: Oversee the operational health, performance, and support of critical North American and global data products, driving incident management, platform availability, and adherence to enterprise service level agreements (SLAs).

What You Bring

Degree and/or diploma in: Computer Science, Data Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related discipline. Master’s degree preferred, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
8-10 years of progressive experience, preferably in: data engineering, data platform, cloud engineering, enterprise data architecture, or related technology leadership roles, including experience managing managers and technical professionals.
Proven experience in cloud-based data architecture and engineering: Deep expertise designing and scaling enterprise data platforms using Google Cloud Platform services such as BigQuery, Cloud Storage, Dataproc, Cloud Data Fusion, Cloud Run, and Apigee.
Strong proficiency in modern engineering practices and tools: Experience with Kubernetes, particularly GKE, microservices architecture, enterprise APIs, serverless computing, infrastructure-as-code using Terraform, Azure DevOps, and CI/CD frameworks.
Strategic understanding of BI, analytics, and artificial intelligence: Knowledge of semantic data models, Looker, Power BI, machine learning pipelines, and AI-driven solutions that accelerate engineering delivery and operational excellence.
Exceptional leadership and communication skills: Ability to influence senior leaders, align cross-functional teams, translate technical strategy into measurable business outcomes, and build a strong culture of accountability and collaboration.
Commercial real estate industry experience: Considered an asset.

This posting is for an existing vacancy within our organization.

Colliers does not use AI-enabled tools to sort or decline applications. All decisions are made by our talent acquisition team.

Innovative projects:
Work on cutting-edge initiatives that shape our communities, drive our growth, and make a tangible impact.

Career growth:
Advance your career and achieve your goals with industry-leading training and development programs.

Competitive benefits & compensation:
Enjoy a comprehensive and flexible benefits package along with competitive compensation that rewards your contributions and supports your well-being.

Collaborative culture:
Join our enterprising team where innovation thrives, collaboration is key, and our people are empowered to be their authentic selves and do their best work.

Diversity, Equity & Inclusion:
Our robust North American Diversity & Inclusion Program features eight Employee Resource Groups (ERGs), where you can connect, learn, and contribute to a diverse and supportive community. Learn more: https://www.collierscanada.com/en-ca/careers/diversity-and-inclusion

Global network
: Join a global team of 28,000 professionals across 70 countries, where you'll expand your network and learn from experts in a dynamic international community. Accelerate your career and enhance your expertise as you connect and collaborate with top talent around the world.

Job Description

What is the opportunity?

The Senior Director-Head of CNB Wealth Business Architecture is a senior leadership role within City National Bank (RBC) Wealth Technology, reporting directly to the Head of CNB Wealth Technology.

The role is responsible for leading the CNB Wealth Business Architecture organization, with approximately 30 professionals, and driving the product strategy, roadmap, prioritization, and execution of technology capabilities that support City National Bank’s Wealth Management business.

The successful candidate will serve as a strategic partner to CNB Wealth business leadership, bringing deep Wealth Management industry expertise and a strong understanding of the products, platforms, workflows, operating models, and client experiences that underpin a modern wealth management organization.

In addition to the functional leadership responsibilities, the individual will serve as the Head of Toronto for CNB Wealth Technology, providing local leadership, employee engagement, talent development, and organizational oversight for the Toronto-based CNB Wealth Technology community.

What will you do?

Wealth Product Leadership

Lead the Wealth Business Architecture organization of approximately 30 professionals, establishing a high-performing, product-oriented culture focused on business outcomes and client value.
Define and execute the Wealth Product Development strategy in partnership with Wealth business leadership and the Head of Wealth Technology.
Own the product development lifecycle from ideation and prioritization through delivery, adoption, and continuous enhancement.
Translate Wealth business strategy and client needs into clear product strategies, roadmaps, priorities, and measurable outcomes.
Establish and maintain a disciplined product prioritization framework that balances strategic initiatives, business growth opportunities, client experience, regulatory requirements, technology modernization, and operational needs.
Ensure product roadmaps are aligned with the broader Wealth Technology strategy and enterprise technology architecture.
Partner closely with Engineering, Architecture, Data, Cybersecurity, Operations, and other technology functions to ensure successful delivery of product capabilities.
Drive transparency into product investment, priorities, dependencies, delivery progress, and business outcomes.
Establish appropriate product management practices, standards, governance, metrics, and operating rhythms across the organization.
Continuously assess opportunities to simplify, modernize, and improve the Wealth technology experience for advisors, clients, and employees.

Wealth Management Domain Leadership

Serve as a subject-matter leader for Wealth Management technology, bringing a deep understanding of the industry’s products, processes, clients, and technology landscape.
Demonstrate strong knowledge of wealth management operating models, including advisor platforms, portfolio management, financial planning, trading, order management, client onboarding, account opening, reporting, performance, billing, custody, and related capabilities.
Understand the needs of advisors, relationship managers, clients, investment professionals, and wealth operations teams.
Partner with Wealth business leaders to identify opportunities where technology can accelerate growth, improve client experience, increase advisor productivity, and enhance operational efficiency.
Bring external Wealth Management industry perspectives and emerging technology trends into the firm’s product strategy.
Ensure product decisions reflect both immediate business needs and the long-term evolution of the Wealth Management industry.

Business Partnership & Strategic Execution

Serve as a trusted technology and product advisor to senior Wealth business leaders.
Establish strong relationships with business product owners and executives, creating a collaborative model between business and technology.
Facilitate strategic discussions around business capabilities, product priorities, investment decisions, and the future-state Wealth technology ecosystem.
Drive alignment across stakeholders and effectively manage competing priorities.
Identify opportunities to leverage technology, data, automation, and AI to improve the Wealth business.
Communicate product strategy, priorities, progress, risks, and outcomes effectively to executive stakeholders.

People & Organizational Leadership

Lead, coach, and develop the Product Development leadership team and broader organization.
Establish a culture of accountability, ownership, collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement.
Build organizational capabilities and develop a strong pipeline of product leadership talent.
Define roles, responsibilities, career paths, and development opportunities within Product Development.
Attract, develop, and retain high-caliber product professionals with strong Wealth Management expertise.
Establish clear performance expectations and measurable objectives for the organization.

Head Of Toronto Responsibilities

As Head of Toronto for CNB Wealth Technology, the individual will provide local leadership and organizational oversight for the Toronto-based CNB Wealth Technology community.

Responsibilities will include:

Serve as the senior local representative for CNB Wealth Technology in Toronto.
Foster a strong culture of collaboration, engagement, inclusion, and accountability across the Toronto technology community.
Partner with functional technology leaders to support talent development, employee engagement, organizational effectiveness, and retention.
Provide local leadership on employee communications, town halls, organizational events, and culture-building activities.
Help establish Toronto as a strong technology talent center for CNB Wealth Technology.
Support recruiting, onboarding, career development, and succession planning for Toronto-based employees.
Identify and address local organizational issues and escalate matters appropriately to functional leadership.
Ensure strong connectivity between Toronto employees and the broader CNB Wealth Technology organization.
Partner with HR and other enterprise functions on location-specific workforce and organizational matters

What do you need to succeed?

Must have

Deep Wealth Management expertise — Extensive knowledge of Wealth Management products, business processes, operating models, client journeys, and technology platforms.
Product leadership — Proven experience building and leading product organizations and establishing effective product management disciplines.
Business orientation — Ability to understand business strategy and translate it into actionable technology product strategies and roadmaps.
Executive presence — Ability to operate confidently with senior Wealth executives and technology leadership.
Strategic thinking — Ability to connect today’s priorities with the longer-term evolution of the Wealth business.
Execution discipline — Proven ability to move from strategy and prioritization to measurable business outcomes.
Influence without authority — Ability to align business and technology stakeholders across organizational boundaries.
People leadership — Demonstrated ability to build high-performing teams, develop leaders, and create an environment where talent thrives.
Change leadership — Experience leading product transformation, technology modernization, and organizational change.

Proven experience leading a substantial Wealth Management product organization.
Demonstrated understanding of Wealth Management technology platforms and the end-to-end advisor and client experience.

new_jobs.description:
About Us

Visa is a world leader in payments technology, facilitating transactions between consumers, merchants, financial institutions and government entities across more than 200 countries and territories, dedicated to uplifting everyone, everywhere by being the best way to pay and be paid.

At Visa, you'll have the opportunity to create impact at scale — tackling meaningful challenges, growing your skills and seeing your contributions impact lives around the world.

Join Visa and do work that matters – to you, to your community, and to the world. Progress starts with you.

Job Description

The Consulting Director will be a key member of Visa Consulting and Analytics (VCA), a team within Visa Advisory Services that drives tangible, impactful and financial results for Visa’s network clients, including both financial services and merchants. Drawing on our expertise in strategy consulting, data analytics, brand management, marketing, operational and macroeconomics, VCA solves the most strategic problems for our clients.

The Canada Consulting Practice within VCA provides consulting and solution services for Visa’s largest issuers, acquirers and fintechs in Canada. The VCA team provides a comprehensive range of consulting services to deliver solutions that address unique challenges in areas such as improving profitability, strategic growth, customer experience, digital payments and managing risk. The Consulting Director will play an important role on a team of experienced strategic consulting professionals by selling, developing, and delivering high impact projects for Visa Canada’s FI partners.

Potential engagements could include market expansion, revenue uplift, segmentation, portfolio management diagnostics, authorization optimization strategies, assessments of digital product and marketing programs, development of new products with implementation roadmaps, and optimizing client customer servicing processes.

We are looking for a highly entrepreneurial, motivated, strategic, analytical individual who will deliver thought leadership, problem diagnostics and high impact solutions to clients. The incumbent must be able to develop enduring relationships with clients and across the Visa organization.

Specific Responsibilities Include

Proactively engage and manage advisory relationship with key clients and Visa client leadership in regular strategic & planning discussions
Cultivate and manage a pipeline of advisory work with clients to meet individual annual sales and project delivery targets
Lead advisory engagements and manage teams in execution of projects and career mentorship
Develop frameworks, approaches, solutions, and recommendations that effectively and efficiently address the most impactful opportunities and challenges
Partner with peers in other functional areas (e.g., marketing, analytics, risk, innovation, data science, product) and across global regional teams to execute projects in ways that leverage the breadth and depth of Visa’s resources
Produce insights and analyses to improve client performance, drive understanding of client issues and provide strategic guidance for client priorities across the payment P&L
Where employee is a subject matter expert, provide knowledge sharing, coaching and training across functional teams and/or regions
Build new scalable solutions, toolkits, best practice documents and consulting approaches that can be applied across VCA practice

Visa requires at least 3 days in office, expectations of these days will be confirmed by your Hiring Manager.

new_jobs.description:
Job Description

What's the opportunity?

We're looking for a product leader to own the roadmap for RBC's internal agentic AI platform end-to-end — from intake and prioritization through delivery and measurement. As Director, Product Strategy & Roadmap, you will decide what ships and when, ground those decisions in user value and adoption evidence, and own the product experience and analytics that make the platform usable and valuable at scale.

You will bring rigour to prioritization, fluency in agentic AI, and the credibility to partner with engineering on how the roadmap gets built — without owning the technical implementation.

Your responsibilities will include:

Roadmap ownership: Maintaining and communicating a rolling 12-month roadmap with clear, evidence-based prioritization rationale
Stakeholder intake: Capturing, assessing, and prioritizing feature requests from business lines, users, and leadership against a consistent value bar
User experience: Owning the end-to-end product experience across the platform — how users discover, adopt, build with, and get value from it — including the self-service builder, templates, and connector catalog as part of a coherent whole.
Product analytics: Building and maintaining adoption dashboards, usage telemetry, and value-realization measurement to drive decisions
Delivery partnership: Partnering with engineering on acceptance criteria, backlog, and delivery quality, staying engaged to protect the user outcome
Responsible AI in practice: Embedding the safety, governance, and transparency standards set by the AI Group's Safety and Responsible AI function into the roadmap and release gates
Market awareness: Conducting competitive and market analysis to inform platform direction

You're our ideal candidate if you:

Have 8+ years of product management experience, including 3+ in AI/ML products or enterprise platforms
Have a strong product-experience and design sensibility — able to shape how users discover, adopt, and succeed with a product, not only what features it has.
Have a deep working understanding of agentic AI: LLMs, tool-use, MCP connectors, RAG, and multi-agent orchestration
Have owned and delivered a product roadmap with measurable adoption outcomes
Are strongly analytical — able to define and track adoption metrics, build dashboards, and interpret telemetry
Have the technical fluency to partner with engineers on architecture decisions without writing code
Have agile delivery expertise: backlog grooming and acceptance-criteria definition
Have financial services awareness, or the ability to develop it quickly - understanding banking end-users (advisors, analysts, operations staff) and their workflow needs

Nice to have:

Bachelor's or Master's in Computer Science, Engineering, Business, HCI, or a related discipline
Product management certification (AIPM, Pragmatic Institute, CSPO, or SAFe)
Experience building developer platforms, APIs, or self-service builder tools
Familiarity with AI governance frameworks (NIST AI RMF, OSFI E-23, or equivalent)
Experience with prompt engineering, model evaluation, or fine-tuning in production
Background at a fintech, regtech, or major bank digital team

What's in it for you:

Drive AI transformation at one of Canada's largest and most respected financial institutions, with exposure to senior leadership across RBC
Be part of a newly formed, high-impact function within RBC's AI Group alongside experienced transformation leaders
A comprehensive Total Rewards Program including bonuses and flexible benefits, competitive compensation, commissions, and stock options where applicable
Leaders who support your development through coaching and managing opportunities
Ability to make a difference and lasting impact from a local-to-global scale

About the AI Group:

RBC's AI Group is the AI accelerator for RBC, with a focus on driving the shift from early-stage AI projects to scaled, client outcomes that amplify the impact of RBC's people. In addition to helping scale the biggest AI opportunities at RBC, the AI Group is responsible for advancing research into emerging use cases across generative and agentic AI, while maintaining expertise in security, responsible AI and regulatory expectations.

Who We Are

For over 30 years, our entrepreneurial mindset and strategic vision have fueled our growth into one of Canada’s largest and most successful REITs. Our retail-focused and mixed-use portfolio reflects our commitment to creating vibrant community spaces where people want to shop, live, work, and play. We take pride in our strong legacy while continuously adapting, innovating, and investing in the future. We’re proud to be recognized as one of Canada’s Most Admired Corporate Cultures, Canada’s Greenest Employers, Canada’s Best Diversity Employers, and a Greater Toronto Top Employer.

At RioCan, we believe our people are our greatest strength. We foster a welcoming, inclusive culture where employees can connect authentically, grow continuously, and bring their whole selves to work. Here, you’ll find opportunities to learn, lead, and make an impact every day.

Purpose of the Position

Reporting to the SLT leadership, the Vice President, Information Technology is accountable for the stability, security, scalability and performance of RioCan's technology environment. The role provides the foundational technology capabilities that enable enterprise operations across infrastructure, cybersecurity, workplace technology, enterprise applications, vendor relationships and technology risk management ensuring systems are secure, resilient, cost effective and aligned with business objectives.

Equally, this is an opportunity to further strengthen technology's role as a strategic partner to the business, building on a solid operational foundation and deepening alignment between technology priorities and enterprise objectives. The Vice President will lead with influence, communicate technology in business language and ensure the technology ecosystem supports growth, operational excellence and innovation while balancing risk, reliability and cost.

Key Responsibilities

Technology Strategy & Architecture

Develop and execute RioCan's technology strategy and roadmap, ensuring technology investments support long-term business objectives
Maintain a scalable, modern and resilient technology architecture built on the organization’s cloud platform
Identify opportunities to simplify and rationalize the application landscape
Evaluate emerging technologies that improve operational effectiveness and the employee experience
Align the work of IT with business priorities through a clear scorecard and a three- to five-year plan

Infrastructure & Operations

Own enterprise infrastructure, networks, cloud platforms, workplace technology and end-user computing
Ensure high levels of system availability, reliability and performance
Establish operational standards and service management practices
Drive continuous improvement of technology services and support
Ensure business continuity and disaster recovery of enterprise IT systems are maintained and tested, in partnership with the functions that own the broader BCP mandate

Cybersecurity & Technology Risk

Lead RioCan's cybersecurity model, protecting company systems, data and users from internal and external threats
Oversee identity and access management, security monitoring, incident response and technology controls, including the maturation of multi-factor authentication and single sign-on
Manage the outsourced security partnership and hold it to leading practice, staying ahead of sector peers
Ensure alignment with regulatory, privacy and risk management requirements, partnering with enterprise risk, legal and compliance on technology-related risks

Enterprise Applications

Oversee enterprise platforms including property operations, leasing, People and Culture, construction and workplace technologies
Own the technology delivery of the enterprise property management platform and the activation of additional modules, partnering with the business on how capability is adopted and used
Ensure systems are reliable, integrated and aligned with business requirements, reducing reliance on spreadsheet-based processes
Support business leaders in maximizing value from technology investments

Service Delivery & Employee Experience

Transform service desk delivery as the most visible face of technology to the business into a highly responsive, measurable, service-oriented function
Establish service levels, reporting and a feedback loop that demonstrably improve end-user satisfaction
Strengthen communication and transparency between IT and the business, building understanding of what technology is delivering and why

Vendor & Partner Management

Develop and manage strategic relationships with technology vendors and service providers, including outsourced application development and managed security partners
Negotiate contracts and service-level agreements and monitor vendor performance and accountability
Ensure technology investments deliver expected value and outcomes

Digital Enablement & Modernization

Partner with business leaders to deliver technology solutions that improve productivity and efficiency, and support enterprise automation initiatives
Identify opportunities to streamline processes through technology
Lead application lifecycle planning and modernization efforts in collaboration with the appropriate business partners
Enable safe, well-governed adoption of AI and productivity tooling across the enterprise, in partnership with the data and analytics function

Leadership

Lead and develop a high-performing technology organization
Foster a culture of accountability, service excellence, innovation and continuous improvement
Build strong succession and talent development plans, establishing and evolving the team over time
Act as a trusted advisor to the senior leadership team on technology opportunities and risks
Build a network of technology leaders, industry peers and professional associations outside the organization, and stay current on emerging technologies, standards and leading practices

Success Factors

Key Success Measures – First 12 to 24 Months

Strong system uptime and service reliability
Improved technology service levels and end-user satisfaction
Reduced cybersecurity risk exposure
Successful execution of technology modernization initiatives
Effective vendor management and cost optimization
Stable and scalable platforms supporting business growth
Enhanced resilience, continuity and disaster recovery capabilities
Clear alignment between technology investments and business priorities

Qualifications

Required

10+ years of progressive technology leadership experience, including leading enterprise IT for a mid-sized to large organization
Experience leading enterprise infrastructure, cybersecurity and applications environments, with proven success managing complex technology ecosystems
Strong understanding of cloud technologies, enterprise architecture, cybersecurity and IT operations
Track record of technology transformation and modernization while balancing the need for operational continuity
Strong vendor management and outsourcing experience, including negotiation of contracts and service levels
Demonstrated ability to partner effectively with business leaders and executive teams, and to communicate technology issues in business language
Track record of building and leading high-performing technical teams

Preferred

Experience partnering with analytics, finance and business leaders in a matrixed environment
Experience in real estate, REIT or other asset-intensive, operationally complex environments; candidates from outside real estate are equally welcome
Familiarity with recognized security control frameworks and the roadmap required to mature between them
Experience enabling enterprise adoption of cloud productivity, AI and business intelligence tooling
A reputation for operational excellence and disciplined execution

Education

Bachelor's degree is required; an advanced degree is highly preferred

Why join RioCan?

We believe in rewarding you for what you do and investing in your career and long-term success. Our total rewards program is designed to help you thrive in every aspect of your life: physically, emotionally, financially, and socially. Here’s what we offer:

An Extensive Health and Benefits Program
that includes health and dental benefits starting on day one, healthcare and wellness/lifestyle spending accounts, access to an employee family and assistance program, virtual healthcare services, and other resources to support your overall well-being.

A Comprehensive Retirement Program
to help prepare you for your future. This includes matching employee contributions in a retirement savings plan, pension plan,

and an employee unit purchase plan.

Work/Life Balance
that prioritizes you. Enjoy flexible work hours, an extra-long weekend with our RioCan Cares Day, and half days before every long weekend in the summer.

Professional Growth and Development
opportunities to advance your skills and grow your career through our continuing education reimbursement, mentorship and leadership development programs, on-demand online learning, and cross-functional training opportunities.

Additional Perks and Benefits
that include paid time off, parental leave top-up, employee discounts, referral and recognition programs, and year-round opportunities to connect through community initiatives, committees, and social events.

If you share RioCan’s values and a passion for real estate, we want to hear from you.

We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive work environment where all employees are valued, included, and empowered to do their best work and bring great ideas. People are at the core of who we are, and we respect that they have taken all paths to get here. Overview

Reporting to CFO Nuclear, this position provides high quality financial support to the overall Nuclear sector. This role will facilitate and analyze budget, actuals, forecasts, revenue processes and objectives to ensure a consistent approach across all sectors.

This is a temporary position to cover a parental leave.

Your role

Lead the Financial Planning and Analysis reporting process for the sector and coordinate with each Business Unit for the consolidated sector-wide actuals, as compared to budgets and quarterly forecasts, as well as the reporting for quarterly forecasts, working with the corporate finance departments to ensure reliable budgets and forecasts are updated.
Coordinate monthly and quarterly closing processes across the sector.
Support the sector as needed, including the development of processes, tools, and reports to help with planning, forecasting and performance monitoring activities.
Review and analyze the monthly, quarterly and yearly performance of the sector versus the budget, forecasts and previous years, explaining what has happened and what is expected to happen.
Review and analyze the long-range plan and budget of the Nuclear central team as well as the Nuclear sector.
Participate in various special projects and ad hoc financial analysis and reporting.
Participate in various tasks related to the reporting of financial information.
Participate in creating and implementing policies and procedures.
Maintain up-to-date sector Levels of Authority.
Establish effective working relationships with colleagues and stakeholders in the Nuclear sector and other corporate finance departments.
Responsible for the Actuals, Budget, Forecast, Long-Range Plan (LRP) and accounting for the Nuclear central team (PMO).
Create operational plans, rolling forecasts and latest estimates.
Lead and coordinate external audits and IFCR processes.
Lead or participate in initiatives that are part of the Finance strategy that impact the effectiveness and efficiency of the Finance function within the Nuclear sector.
This role can be based in Montreal or Mississauga.
Occasional travel.

About You

Professional accounting designation with a minimum of 7 years of finance or accounting experience.
Understanding of accounting processes and IFRS policies.
Ability to take initiative and work independently.
Ability to manage competing deadlines and balance priorities.
Team player with strong leadership skills and ability to influence.
Strong organizational skills and the ability to effectively multitask.
Oriented towards teamwork and ability to communicate and work with other members of the organization.
Strong consulting and problem-solving skills.
Flexibility to accommodate work demands.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English and French; the role supports teams across Canada and internationally.

Rewards & benefits

Enjoy competitive compensation, employee recognition, and a brilliant range of flexible benefits you can tailor to your health, wellbeing, financial and lifestyle needs.

Be rewarded. Find out more.

- Diriger la fonction comptable et financière, en veillant à l'exactitude et à la ponctualité des rapports financiers.
- Superviser les clôtures de fin de mois et de fin d'exercice, y compris les rapprochements de comptes et la préparation des états financiers.
- Élaborer des budgets, des prévisions et des projections de flux de trésorerie pour soutenir la planification d'affaires.
- Analyser le rendement financier, cerner les écarts et formuler des recommandations visant à améliorer la rentabilité.
- Gérer les activités de trésorerie, les flux de trésorerie et les engagements financiers de l'organisation.
- Coordonner les audits externes, les conseillers fiscaux et les autres fournisseurs de services professionnels.
- Agir à titre de partenaire d'affaires de confiance auprès de l'équipe de direction en matière de stratégie financière, d'investissements et d'initiatives de croissance.
- Renforcer les contrôles internes, rationaliser les processus et améliorer l'efficacité opérationnelle.
- Superviser l'équipe comptable tout en appuyant les activités administratives liées aux ressources humaines.
- Collaborer avec des spécialistes en technologie, tant à l'interne qu'à l'externe, pour améliorer les systèmes ERP et financiers.

- Titre de CPA et diplôme universitaire en comptabilité, en finance ou dans un domaine connexe.

- Expérience dans la direction d'équipes interfonctionnelles et la collaboration avec des cadres supérieurs.
- Connaissances avancées des systèmes ERP et des logiciels comptables.
- Excellentes compétences analytiques, organisationnelles et de résolution de problèmes.
- Capacité à traduire des données financières complexes en recommandations opérationnelles concrètes.

- Salaire concurrentiel : 150 000 $ à 170 000 $
- Environnement de travail hybride
- Poste de direction offrant une grande autonomie et une visibilité auprès de la haute direction
- Perspective de carrière à long terme au sein d'une organisation en pleine croissance
